mainTopic: תקנת השבים when the stolen item exists, and whether רבי מאיר's ruling on wool and offspring is a קנס (and whether it applies to a שוגג)
overview: The גמרא first settles a contradiction between two ברייתות about accepting stolen property back from a robber who repents. If the stolen item still exists (גזילה קיימת), it is returned. If it is gone, תקנת השבים says the victim should not take payment. The גמרא tests this with the story of the belt (אבנט), which it reads as the belt's value. It also tests it with the stolen beam (מריש) built into a building, which the Sages treat as if it no longer exists. Then the גמרא turns to our משנה about a stolen pregnant cow and a ewe that was sheared. It brings a ברייתא with the views of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. It asks whether רבי מאיר makes the robber return the wool and offspring because a change does not transfer ownership, or because of a קנס. A proof from aged animals and slaves is rejected, but the case of the dyer who used the wrong color proves it is a קנס. A second version says this was always clear and asks instead whether the קנס also applies to a robber who acted by mistake (שוגג). The גמרא starts a proof from a ברייתא about claims collected only from unsold property, and that proof continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Two different cases: stolen item still exists or not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction between the two ברייתות by saying one speaks of a stolen item that still exists, and the other of one that no longer exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, the stolen item still exists. There, the stolen item no longer exists.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between two ברייתות about whether we accept stolen property back from a penitent robber. It says each ברייתא is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stolen item is still there, the victim may take it back, because the robber must return it no matter what. If the item is gone and only money is owed, the Sages' enactment for penitents (תקנת השבים) says not to accept payment, so robbers will not be scared away from repenting.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (in this case / this ברייתא)
The stolen item still exists
The stolen item no longer exists

steps.confusionAlert: The two כאן's point to two different ברייתות. They are not two halves of one ruling. Each one is a separate case.

phrases.english: Here, where the stolen item still exists;
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says you may accept what the robber returns.

phrases.english: there, where the stolen item no longer exists.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן בִּגְזֵילָה קַיֶּימֶת, כָּאן בְּשֶׁאֵין גְּזֵילָה קַיֶּימֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves a contradiction raised just before this section on the previous עמוד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא refers to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to argue about whether to accept anything from a penitent robber
steps.terutzMaskana: We accept the item if it still exists. We refuse money payment if the item is gone.

steps.title: Challenge from the story of the belt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the belt in the story that triggered תקנת השבים was still in existence.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the belt was a stolen item that still existed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 1. In the famous story that led to תקנת השבים, the robber was told he must return even his belt, and that belt still existed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תקנת השבים only applies when the stolen item is gone, it would not help a robber whose belt still exists. Yet the belt story is the very reason the enactment was made. So the answer from Step 1 seems to clash with the enactment's own origin.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! (opens a challenge)
Belt

phrases.english: But the belt —
phrases.notes: This is the story of the robber whose wife told him that even his belt was not his, so he gave up on repenting.

phrases.english: it is a stolen item that still exists!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַבְנֵט דִּגְזֵילָה קַיֶּימֶת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in Step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תקנת השבים applies only when the stolen item no longer exists
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story that caused the enactment involved a belt that still existed, so the enactment must cover existing items too

steps.title: The belt means the value of the belt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'belt' in the story means the money value of the belt, not the belt itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'belt' mean? The value of the belt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the story differently. The belt itself was gone, and the robber only owed its value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we say the robber owed money for the belt, the story fits Step 1 well. It is a case where the stolen item no longer exists, which is exactly where תקנת השבים applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What (is meant by)?
The value / money worth of

phrases.english: What is meant by "belt"?
The value of the belt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אַבְנֵט דְּמֵי אַבְנֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The robber had to return the actual belt, which still existed
steps.terutzMaskana: He owed only the belt's value, so the item no longer existed and Step 1 stands

steps.title: Challenge from the stolen beam built into a building
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: in the case of a stolen beam built into a building, the beam still exists, yet the Sages made תקנת השבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that wherever the stolen item still exists, the Sages made no enactment? But a beam still exists, and we learned: with a stolen beam that he built into a building, the owner takes its value, because of the enactment for penitents!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question on the rule from Step 1. It quotes a משנה about a stolen beam (מריש), which still exists, yet the Sages applied תקנת השבים to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beam is physically still there inside the building. Even so, the משנה lets the robber pay its value instead of tearing down his building. That looks like תקנת השבים working even when the item exists, which goes against Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: An enactment made by the Sages
A beam
A building (literally, a large building or castle)
The Sages' enactment to make repentance easier for robbers
And we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: And anywhere that the stolen item still exists,
the Sages did not make an enactment?!
But there is a beam, which is a stolen item that still exists;
and we learned: regarding the stolen beam
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in גיטין 55a.

phrases.english: that he built into a building,
that the owner takes its value
because of the enactment for penitents!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דִּגְזֵילָה קַיֶּימֶת לָא עֲבוּד רַבָּנַן תַּקַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the distinction from Step 1, this time from a משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that תקנת השבים does not apply where the stolen item exists
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The beam exists, yet the משנה applies תקנת השבים to it

steps.title: The beam is treated as if it no longer exists
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that because removing the beam would destroy the building, the Sages treated the beam as if it were gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there. Since there would be a loss of the building, the Sages treated the beam as though it does not exist.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the beam challenge. It says the beam case is special, because taking out the beam would ruin the whole building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beam still counts as a stolen item. But because of the heavy loss, the Sages ruled it should be treated like an item that no longer exists. So the beam case fits into the 'no longer exists' side of Step 1 and does not break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
A loss
As though it does not exist

steps.whatToRemember: תקנת השבים applies when the stolen item is gone. A beam built into a building is treated as gone because of the great loss that taking it out would cause.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since there is a loss of the building,
the Sages treated it as though it does not exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּכֵיוָן דְּאִיכָּא פְּסֵידָא דְבִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4 and closes the discussion
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special case: the item exists but is treated as gone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The beam case shows תקנת השבים applies even to existing items
steps.terutzMaskana: The beam is treated as nonexistent because of the loss to the building, so Step 1's rule holds

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a stolen pregnant cow that gave birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה about a stolen pregnant cow that gave birth, to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He stole a pregnant cow and it gave birth, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting our משנה. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the robber pays the value the animal had when it was stolen, a pregnant cow or an unshorn ewe. The גמרא is about to bring a ברייתא with other opinions on this case.

keyTerms.meaning: He stole (by robbery)
Pregnant
Etc. (the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: He stole a pregnant cow and it gave birth, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּזַל פָּרָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת וְיָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on a different line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The robber pays the animal's value at the time of the theft (as the משנה teaches)

steps.title: Three views on paying for wool and offspring
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings three opinions on a stolen ewe that was sheared or a cow that gave birth: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One who steals a ewe and shears it, or a cow and it gives birth, pays back the animal, its wool, and its offspring. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: the stolen item goes back as it is. רבי שמעון says: we view it as if it had been valued in money while with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three opinions on what the robber owes when the stolen animal grew wool or had a baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the owner gets everything: the animal, the wool, and the offspring. רבי יהודה says the item is returned in whatever state it is now. רבי שמעון says we treat the animal as if its price was fixed at the time of theft, so the robber pays only that amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
A ewe (female sheep)
Its shorn wool
Its offspring
Is returned as it is
Valued / appraised

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not mean the robber returns the animal's current value. He means its value is fixed at the time of the theft, as if it had been priced then.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who steals a ewe and shears it,
a cow and it gives birth —
pays it and its shorn wool
and its offspring; the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: גְּזֵילָה חוֹזֶרֶת בְּעֵינֶיהָ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: A stolen item is returned as it is.
Rabbi Shimon says: We view it
as if it were valued in money while with him.
phrases.notes: He means its price was locked in when it was stolen, so the robber pays only that price.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הַגּוֹזֵל רָחֵל וּגְזָזָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה quoted in Step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: return the animal, wool, and offspring. רבי יהודה: return as is. רבי שמעון: pay its value from the time of theft.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר makes the robber return the wool and offspring: does a change not transfer ownership, or is this a fine?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was asked of them: What is רבי מאיר's reason? Is it because he holds that a change stays in its place? Or perhaps he generally holds that a change acquires, and here he is imposing a fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the reason behind רבי מאיר's view in the ברייתא. It gives two possible reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: רבי מאיר holds that a change (שינוי) does not give the robber ownership, so the wool and offspring still belong to the owner. Option two: he agrees that a change normally gives the robber ownership, but here he fines the robber and makes him give them back anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them (a question the Sages raised)
A change in the item
Stays in its place (does not change ownership)
A change gives the robber ownership
A fine / penalty

steps.whyThisMatters: The two reasons give the same result here but say different things about רבי מאיר's general view on whether a change transfers ownership, which matters in other cases of theft.

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
What is Rabbi Meir's reason?
Is it because he holds:
a change stays in its place?
phrases.notes: In other words, even after the animal changed, it still belongs to the owner.

phrases.english: Or perhaps, generally a change acquires,
and here it is a fine that he imposes?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reason behind רבי מאיר's view in the ברייתא of Step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר's ruling comes from holding that a change does not transfer ownership, or from a fine on the robber

steps.title: What practical difference do the two reasons make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case it would matter whether רבי מאיר's reason is 'a change does not transfer ownership' or 'a fine'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: Before trying to answer Step 8's question, the גמרא asks why it matters at all. This sets up the next line, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons lead to the same result for the wool and offspring, since the owner gets them back either way. So the גמרא wants a case where the two reasons would give different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference?

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the two-sided question of Step 8 matters in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two possible reasons for רבי מאיר would lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: when the stolen item lost value
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up when the stolen item became worth less after the robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a case where it lost value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the two reasons differ when the stolen item dropped in value while it was with the robber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose a change does not transfer ownership. Then the item still belongs to the owner, and the robber can hand it back as it is, even though it is now worth less. Suppose instead the robber really acquired it, and returning it is only a fine. Then he must pay what it was worth when he stole it.

keyTerms.meaning: It lost value / became weaker

phrases.english: For where it became weakened (lost value).

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהֵיכָא דִּכְחַשָׁה מִכְחָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the item lost value: if 'change doesn't acquire', it is returned as is. If it is a fine, the robber pays its value at the time of the robbery.

steps.title: Bringing a משנה about stolen animals and slaves that grew old
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if a stolen animal or slaves grew old, the robber pays their value at the time of the robbery. רבי מאיר says slaves can be returned as they are. This implies that for an animal, even רבי מאיר says to pay the original value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone robbed an animal and it grew old, or slaves and they grew old, he pays what they were worth at the time of the robbery. רבי מאיר says: with slaves, he tells the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you.' But for an animal, he pays its value at the time of the robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to try to answer Step 8's question. Here it only lays out the source. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Growing old is a change that lowers value. This is exactly the case from Step 10. רבי מאיר only argues about slaves, so it seems that for an animal he agrees the robber pays the original value.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source is being brought as proof)
It grew old
According to its value at the time of the robbery
Here is yours before you (take it back as it is)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he robbed an animal and it grew old,
or slaves and they grew old,
he pays according to the time of the robbery.
רבי מאיר says,
with slaves, he says to him: 'Here is yours before you.'
whereas an animal – according to the time of the robbery;
phrases.notes: This line is the גמרא's own inference, not part of the משנה: רבי מאיר only argued about slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: גָּזַל בְּהֵמָה וְהִזְקִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the case Step 10 identified, an item that lost value.
steps.raayaObject: Which side of Step 8's question רבי מאיר holds
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a stolen animal or slaves that grew old

steps.title: So רבי מאיר holds that a change transfers ownership
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר held that a changed item stays the owner's, he would let the robber return the aged animal too. Since he doesn't, he must hold שינוי קונה. That would mean returning the wool and offspring is a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think רבי מאיר holds a change leaves the item where it was, then even an animal should be returned as is! Rather, doesn't this prove that רבי מאיר holds a change acquires, and here, with the wool and offspring, it is a fine he imposes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion from the משנה. רבי מאיר makes the robber pay the original value for an aged animal, so he must think the change gave the robber ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 showed the test case. If change doesn't acquire, the item goes back as is. If it does acquire, the robber pays the old value. רבי מאיר says to pay the old value for an animal, which fits 'change acquires'. So the wool and offspring rule must be a fine.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you were to think)
The changed item stays in its place (still belongs to the owner)
A change transfers ownership to the robber
A fine / penalty

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר שִׁינּוּי בִּמְקוֹמוֹ עוֹמֵד,
phrases.english: that רבי מאיר holds a change stays in its place,
then even an animal too!
phrases.notes: He means the aged animal should also just be handed back as it is.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that we learn from this,
that רבי מאיר holds a change acquires –
and here it is a fine that he imposes?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the shearing and birth case from Step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ סָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר שִׁינּוּי בִּמְקוֹמוֹ עוֹמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds שינוי קונה and that returning wool and offspring is a קנס
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's ruling that an aged animal is paid for at its value at the time of the robbery

steps.title: רבי מאיר was only arguing on the חכמים' terms
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. In his own view, רבי מאיר says change doesn't acquire, even for an animal. He only argued about slaves to tell the חכמים: even by your view, a slave is like land, and land can't be stolen. The חכמים reply that a slave is like movable property.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: רבי מאיר was speaking to the חכמים according to their own view. 'For me, a change does not acquire, even for an animal. But according to you, who say a change acquires, at least agree with me about a slave, who is like land, and land cannot be stolen!' And the חכמים answered him: 'No, a slave is like movable property.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from Step 12. רבי מאיר's silence about animals doesn't show his own view. He was only arguing with the חכמים using their own starting point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Personally, רבי מאיר could hold that a change never acquires, so even an aged animal goes back as is. He picked slaves because he hoped the חכמים would agree with him there, since slaves are like land, and land always stays the owner's. The חכמים disagreed, so this source cannot settle Step 8's question. The גמרא tries another source in Step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their words (arguing from the other side's view)
According to me / according to you
Land cannot be stolen (it always stays the owner's)
Movable property

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי מאיר agrees that an animal is paid at its old value. In this answer, that was only the חכמים' view. He used it as a starting point to argue about slaves.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the aging משנה fails, because רבי מאיר may have been speaking לדבריהם דרבנן. The גמרא settles the question with a different source in Steps 14-16.

phrases.english: They say,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ:
phrases.english: רבי מאיר was speaking to them according to the words of the חכמים:
According to me – a change does not acquire,
and even an animal too.
phrases.notes: He means that in his own view, even the aged animal goes back as it is.

phrases.english: But according to you, who say a change acquires –
at least agree with me about a slave,
since he is like land,
and land cannot be stolen!
And the חכמים said to him:
No, a slave is like movable property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי, רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 12 by reading רבי מאיר's statement differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the aging משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי מאיר's words show his own view on animals. He may only have been arguing from the חכמים' view, while personally holding that change never acquires.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common tool of the גמרא: a תנא may say something only to argue within his opponent's view, so his words don't always show his own opinion.

steps.title: A new proof from the dyer who used the wrong color
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a dyer was told to dye wool red and dyed it black, or the reverse. רבי מאיר says he pays the owner the value of the wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone gave wool to be dyed red and the dyer dyed it black, or black and he dyed it red, רבי מאיר says the dyer gives the owner the value of his wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to answer the open question about רבי מאיר's reasoning. This step only quotes the source; the next step draws the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the wool's color is a change (שינוי) to the item. רבי מאיר's ruling on what the dyer must pay will show whether he thinks a change transfers ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening for bringing a proof from a source
To dye
The value of his wool

phrases.english: Come and hear:
[If one gave wool to a dyer] to dye it red for him, and he dyed it black,
[or to dye it] black, and he dyed it red –

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: נוֹתֵן לוֹ דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: he gives him the value of his wool.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in steps 11-12 was rejected in step 13, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי מאיר holds שינוי קונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the dyer who dyed the wool the wrong color

steps.title: The dyer pays only for the plain wool, so the change made it his
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says only 'the value of his wool', not the wool plus its added value from the dye. If change did not transfer ownership, the dyer would have to give back the wool with its added value.
steps.simpleTranslation: The value of his wool, yes; the value of the wool and its improvement, no. If you thought רבי מאיר holds a change does not transfer ownership, the dyer would have to give the owner the wool's value together with its improvement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from the dyer משנה. Since the dyer pays only for plain wool, the dyed wool must now belong to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שינוי אין קונה, the dyed wool would still be the owner's, and he would receive it with its added value. Since רבי מאיר gives the owner only the original wool's value, he must hold that the change made the wool the dyer's.

keyTerms.meaning: Its improvement, the extra value added (here, by the dye)
If it enters your mind, introducing an idea that will be shown wrong
A change does not transfer ownership

phrases.english: The value of his wool – yes,
the value of his wool and its improvement – no;
and if it should enter your mind

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר שִׁינּוּי אֵין קוֹנֶה,
phrases.english: that Rabbi Meir holds a change does not acquire,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ וְשִׁבְחוֹ בָּעֵי לְמִיתַּב לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: he would need to give him the value of his wool and its improvement!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ – אִין, דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ וְשִׁבְחוֹ – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact wording 'דמי צמרו' (and not 'צמרו ושבחו') in רבי מאיר's ruling

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי מאיר holds a change acquires, so returning wool and offspring is a fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי מאיר holds שינוי קונה. So his ruling that a robber returns the wool and offspring must be a קנס, and the גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that רבי מאיר holds a change transfers ownership, and here it is a fine he imposes? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the dyer proof to the original question. It concludes that רבי מאיר's reason is a קנס, and confirms it with 'שמע מינה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By law, the change should have made the wool and offspring the robber's. רבי מאיר still makes him give them back to punish him, so he does not profit from his robbery.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so: introducing the conclusion the גמרא is pushing toward
A change transfers ownership
A fine or penalty imposed by the חכמים
Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, the dyer case proves רבי מאיר holds שינוי קונה. His ruling that the robber returns the wool and offspring is a קנס, not the basic law.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so – learn from this,
that Rabbi Meir holds a change acquires,
and here it is a fine that he imposes?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the original case: the robber who sheared the stolen animal or whose stolen animal gave birth.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the inference from step 15 into the answer to the question from step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר holds שינוי קונה, and returning the wool and offspring is a קנס.

steps.title: Another version: this was never in doubt, because רב reversed the opinions
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבי מאיר's reason was never a question. רב taught the משנה about aged animals and slaves reversed: רבי מאיר says pay the value at the time of the robbery for both. That clearly means שינוי קונה, so returning the wool and offspring is a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: this was never a question for us, since רב reversed the opinions and taught: 'If he stole a cow and it grew old, or slaves and they grew old, he pays their value at the time of the robbery. This is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say: with slaves, he says to the owner, here is yours in front of you.' So certainly רבי מאיר holds a change acquires, and in our case it is a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the whole discussion. In this version, everyone already knew רבי מאיר's reason was a קנס, because of how רב taught the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's version, רבי מאיר makes the robber pay the old value even for slaves, with no exception. Paying the old value shows the change gave the robber ownership, which means שינוי קונה. This also removes the rejection in step 13, which depended on רבי מאיר being the one who spoke about slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say: introducing a second version of the discussion
He reversed, switched which opinion belongs to whom
According to the value at the time of the robbery
Here is yours in front of you: return the item as it is now

steps.confusionAlert: In the regular משנה (step 11), רבי מאיר is the one who says slaves are returned as they are. רב switches the names, so here that line belongs to the חכמים.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
This – was not a question for us;
since Rav reversed [the opinions] and taught:
"If one stole a cow and it grew old,
[or] slaves and they grew old –
he pays [their value] as at the time of the robbery,
this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say: with slaves –
he says to him: here is yours before you" –
certainly, according to Rabbi Meir, a change acquires,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא קְנָסָא הוּא דְּקָא קָנֵיס לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and here it is a fine that he imposes on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: הָא – לָא אִיבְּעִי לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the whole discussion from step 8 onward, in which רבי מאיר's reason was never in doubt.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר holds שינוי קונה, so returning wool and offspring is a קנס
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's reversed version of the משנה about a stolen animal and slaves that grew old

steps.title: The real question: does רבי מאיר fine a robber who acted by mistake?
steps.stepSummary: In this version, the question was whether רבי מאיר's קנס applies only to a robber who acted on purpose (מזיד), or also to one who acted by mistake (שוגג).
steps.simpleTranslation: When we asked, this is what we asked: when רבי מאיר fines, is it only someone who acted on purpose, and not someone who acted by mistake? Or perhaps he fines even someone who acted by mistake?
steps.whatsHappening: The second version now states what the real question was. It is not about רבי מאיר's reason, which is already settled as a קנס, but about how far the fine reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fine is usually meant to punish wrongdoing on purpose, so maybe it does not apply when someone took the item by mistake. On the other hand, רבי מאיר might fine even a mistake so people will be more careful. Step 19 brings a source to try to answer this.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who acts on purpose, knowing it is wrong
Someone who acts by mistake, without knowing
Or perhaps: introducing the second side of a question

phrases.english: When we asked [the question] –
this is what we asked:
when he imposes a fine – is it [only] for one who acted intentionally,
but for one who acted unintentionally he does not fine;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא אֲפִילּוּ בְּשׁוֹגֵג נָמֵי קָנֵיס?
phrases.english: or perhaps he fines even one who acted unintentionally as well?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא אִיבְּעִי לַן – הָכִי אִיבְּעִי לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Inside the second version, replaces the original question from step 8 with a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר's קנס applies only to a מזיד robber, or also to a שוגג

steps.title: A ברייתא listing five claims collected only from unsold property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists five kinds of claims that can only be collected from property the debtor still owns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: five kinds of claims are collected only from unsold property. They are: produce, the improvement of produce, a man who agreed to feed his wife's son or daughter, a loan document with no property guarantee, and a woman's כתובה with no property guarantee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a proof for the question from step 18 by quoting a ברייתא. Right now it is only laying out the source; the proof itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a creditor can take back land the debtor sold to someone else. This ברייתא lists five claims that are weaker: they can only be collected from land the debtor still holds. One item, 'the improvement of produce,' will turn out to be the key to the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer a question
Free, unsold property that the debtor still owns
The improvement or added value of produce
A property guarantee: the clause saying all the debtor's land backs the debt
A woman's marriage contract, which promises her money

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Five types of claims are collected only from unsold property,
phrases.notes: 'Unsold property' means land the debtor still owns, not land he already sold to someone else.

phrases.english: and these are they: produce, and the improvement of produce,
and one who takes upon himself to feed
his wife's son or his wife's daughter,
and a loan document that has no property guarantee,
and a woman's marriage contract that has no property guarantee.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: חֲמִשָּׁה גּוֹבִין מִן הַמְחוֹרָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to answer the שוגג/מזיד question raised in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי מאיר's קנס applies to a robber who acted by mistake (שוגג)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing five claims collected only from unsold property

steps.title: This ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, because only he holds that a missing guarantee clause is not a scribe's mistake. So the item 'improvement of produce' is also his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who do we know says that a missing guarantee clause is not a scribe's mistake? רבי מאיר. And this ברייתא teaches 'produce and the improvement of produce.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out whose opinion the ברייתא follows, and finds it is רבי מאיר. This matters because our question is about רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say a loan document without a guarantee clause is treated as if it had one, because leaving it out was the scribe's mistake. רבי מאיר says that if it is missing, there is no guarantee. Since the ברייתא says such a document collects only from unsold property, it must be רבי מאיר, so his view also includes the law about 'improvement of produce.'

keyTerms.meaning: A scribe's mistake
Whom have you heard say this? The גמרא uses it to identify the author of a teaching
And it teaches: points to the part of the source that matters for the proof

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says:
that a missing guarantee is not a scribe's mistake?
Rabbi Meir;
and it teaches: produce and the improvement of produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר: אַחְרָיוּת – לָאו טָעוּת סוֹפֵר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ברייתא from step 19 as רבי מאיר, so it can be used for a question about his view.
steps.raayaObject: That the ruling on 'improvement of produce' is רבי מאיר's view
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling about a loan document with no guarantee, which matches only רבי מאיר

steps.title: What case is 'improvement of produce'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means by 'improvement of produce.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'improvement of produce'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the case behind the phrase 'improvement of produce.' This sets up the case it will use for the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is short and unclear. The proof depends on who pays for the improvement and why, so the גמרא first needs to describe the exact case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? A request to describe the exact situation

phrases.english: The improvement of produce: what is the case?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבַח פֵּירוֹת הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Zooms in on the item from step 20 that will carry the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case meant by 'improvement of produce'

steps.title: A stolen field sold and then improved by the buyer
steps.stepSummary: The case: a robber stole a field and sold it. The buyer improved it, and then the real owner took the field back from the buyer. The גמרא begins to describe what the buyer collects from the robber.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, someone stole a field from another person and sold it to a third person. The buyer improved the field, and now the field is being taken away from him. When the buyer collects from the robber...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by describing the case. The sentence about how the buyer collects from the robber continues after this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real owner proves in court that the field is his and takes it back, together with its improvement. So the buyer loses both the field and the work he put into it, and he turns to the robber who sold it to him. How he collects, and from which property, is the next part of the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbed, took by force
He improved it and raised its value
It is taken out of his possession
Collects payment

phrases.english: For example, where one robbed a field from his fellow
and sold it to another, and he improved it,
phrases.notes: The one who improved it is the buyer, not the robber.

phrases.english: and now it is leaving his possession.
phrases.notes: The real owner proved the field is his, so it is taken from the buyer.

phrases.english: When he collects,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the buyer collecting from the robber. The sentence finishes in the next lines of the גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁגָּזַל שָׂדֶה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ וּמְכָרָהּ לְאַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by giving the case of 'improvement of produce'; the explanation continues past this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a stolen field that was sold and then improved by the buyer, and later taken back by the real owner. The buyer then collects from the robber.
